fatal_errors: The proposed Al 2024 material system is unrelated to the target HfMoTaTiZr refractory high-entropy alloy.
Standard Al 2024 does not contain sufficient scandium to form Al3Sc precipitates; no Sc-alloying intervention is specified.
The intervention omits the target addition of 4.2 at.% Cr and the resulting reticulated multicomponent Laves phase.
The proposed mechanism does not capture the target combination of Cr-induced solid-solution hardening and crack hindrance by an interconnected Laves-phase network.
No supporting evidence is cited for the asserted numerical improvements.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the broad concept of simultaneous strength and ductility improvement through microstructural engineering, but it does not reconstruct the target method, material, conditions, or mediator. Its central premise is also internally problematic: aging ordinary 2024-T6 aluminum cannot produce coherent Al3Sc precipitates unless scandium was previously added, and T6 already denotes a solution-treated and artificially aged condition. Tensile comparison could test the claimed macroscopic outcome, but without microscopy or compositional analysis it cannot verify precipitate formation, coherence, size, or the proposed mechanism. The target instead relies on Cr addition to HfMoTaTiZr, producing lattice contraction and a low-volume-fraction reticulated Laves phase that jointly raises yield strength and fracture strain.
